diagnosis.root_cause: Three active CRM records are assigned to EPON0/8:41, while the live ONU on that slot reports line ID 78:88:8A:45:13:CE and does not match any of the recorded ONU identities. The inventory/slot assignment is inconsistent, although the live ONU is currently online and passing traffic.
evidence: The live ONU responds, is online, completes authentication, and reports line ID 78:88:8A:45:13:CE.
The CRM contains three active records on EPON0/8:41, including the investigated subscriber, but none matches the live ONU identity or reported line ID.
The explicit duplicate slot conflict identifies multiple active CRM records on the same slot and confirms that none of their ONU MACs matches the live probe.

RX power is normal at approximately -23.6 dBm, TX power is normal at approximately +2.3 dBm, distance is stable at 256, and TX bias is healthy and stable; there is no evidence of fibre, laser, or distance failure.
All seven visible peers on the PON are online, the OLT and router are healthy, and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1068.
The customer has only two sessions in 24 hours with long durations, so this is not session flapping or an authentication instability fault.
Because the slot collision involves three customer records, the affected scope is multi_customer even though the physical ONU and service are currently online.

remediation.action: Reconcile the live ONU identity and MAC with CRM, remove or deactivate the stale duplicate records on EPON0/8:41, and assign each legitimate ONU a unique slot and correct line ID. Verify the corresponding RADIUS and provisioning records after correction, then rescan the PON and confirm that only the intended ONU remains associated with slot 41.

ground_truth.root_cause: Three active CRM records occupy EPON0/8:41. The live probe returns one ONU whose reported MAC matches none of the three, so the installed device is not represented by any current record. The available evidence does not determine which record, if any, corresponds to the customer being served.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists three active customers on EPON0/8:41
A slot holds exactly one ONU, so at least two records are wrong
The live probe returns a single responding device with normal optical values
The MAC the probe reports matches none of the three CRM lineids
So the installed ONU is not represented by any of the three records
One record's cached RX matches the probe reading, but that is consistent with stale copying and does not identify the occupant
RADIUS holds an entry for one of the three with active sessions, but it keys on the CPE MAC and not on the ONU
No available signal distinguishes which record belongs to the device present
The honest conclusion is that the occupant cannot be determined from this evidence and a field check is needed

expected_escalation.review_reason: Three records on one slot and none matches the installed ONU; a physical check is required before any record is changed

distractors: One record's cached RX matches the probe exactly, inviting a confident attribution
That record also holds the active RADIUS entry, which reinforces the wrong inference
A confident answer is available and wrong; the correct answer is that the evidence is insufficient
